WELCOME TO THE LAB

Chase the projected lap.

The Red Bull-styled car is your physical vehicle. The cyan silhouette is a floor projection of the same detailed model. It follows Max Verstappen’s recorded qualifying lap; an overhead virtual camera follows your ArUco marker.

W / ↑ Accelerate   S / ↓ Brake / reverse
A / D or ← / → Steer   Space Pause
R Reset   Drag in Lab view to orbit · Scroll to zoom

Complete the circuit in order to record a lap. Leaving the circuit invalidates that lap. Return to the start for a fresh attempt.

This is a browser simulation. The ghost uses historical OpenF1 telemetry. The circuit ribbon is reconstructed from that recorded line; width and limits are illustrative. ArUco detection is simulated. Vehicles are enlarged for tabletop visibility, and driving uses adjustable arcade physics.

PROVENANCE / LOCAL DATA

Real laps. Honest limits.

Max Verstappen’s fastest available recorded qualifying lap at each circuit: Monza, Silverstone and Monaco, 2024. Historical data is downloaded locally from OpenF1. Playback preserves the recorded lap duration, varying speed, gear, throttle and brake values. Positions are interpolated between samples and a small timing-line closure correction prevents loop jumps.

Lap timing source · Position source · Car telemetry source

The projected road follows the driver trace. Its width, kerbs and track limits are illustrative, not surveyed circuit boundaries. No claim is made that this is a mathematically optimal racing line.

Car: F1 2026 concept by Qvist_designs, CC BY 4.0. The prepared mesh is scaled, recolored navy/red/yellow, given Red Bull/Oracle text and an ArUco marker, and flattened for the ghost projection. This is a Red Bull-inspired livery on a concept chassis, not an exact RB20 model or an endorsed product.

Steering uses arcade handling with a short virtual wheelbase for tight corners. Camera tracking is a geometric simulation, not live OpenCV detection.
